calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Golden Knights are the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Devils’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Golden Knights.

calls.head: Matchup-hunting season
calls.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending Hertl’s line (Connelly, Hertl and Bowman) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Devils’ fourth line is Lombardi, Glass and Brown.
calls.call: The Golden Knights’ L3 (Connelly, Hertl and Bowman) spends at least 30% of its 5-on-5 time against the Devils’ fourth line, against about 21% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 39% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against fourth lines, about 21% with no line matching

With no line matching, this group would face fourth lines about 21% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

surprises.head: Vegas brought the hits
surprises.body: Vegas usually hits less than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 181 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 91 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

story.head: Jack Hughes has two goals as the Devils beat the Golden Knights
paras: It was a busy first period. Luke Hughes got the scoring started for the Devils early in the period. Mark Stone and Ivan Barbashev scored a minute and a half apart late in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead, and that was all they would get. Arseny Gritsyuk tied it up for New Jersey 54 seconds later, and Jack Hughes put the Devils ahead 3-2 early in the second. Gritsyuk struck again late in the period to make it 4-2. Jack Hughes struck again into the empty net with just under three minutes left.

The Golden Knights were outshot 32-21, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. Connor Hellebuyck made 19 saves for the Devils, and Adin Hill stopped 27 of 31 at the other end. The Devils moved to 9-5-0 and climbed to second in the Metropolitan, while the Knights dropped to 9-5-1, second in the Pacific.
